text:
sam_support: Heads-up — Customer AcmeCorp reports their internal endpoint billing.api.private.example.com suddenly returning NXDOMAIN from their app VPC after a routine infra change. They say external resolver still returns the correct IP.
jen_dev: ugh. any errors from their app or curl?
sam_support: customer ran: `dig +short billing.api.private.example.com @10.0.1.2` -> no output (NXDOMAIN). From their forwarder (`10.0.0.2`) it returns `10.10.10.45`. They included traceroute to 10.10.10.45 which times out.
mike_ops: can you ask them for `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name example.com` in their infra account? i suspect duplicate private hosted zones across accounts.
sam_support: they ran it, output shows two private hosted zones for example.com: hz-AAAA (account infra-shared, associated with vpc-11111) and hz-BBBB (account prod, associated with vpc-22222). Their app is in vpc-22222 but the wrong hz (hz-AAAA) is currently also associated via recent cross-account assoc.
alice_sre: that explains split-horizon. Route53 picks the hosted zone with the earliest creation / association precedence? in cross-account setups you can accidentally shadow records. customer probably associated the shared hz to their VPC by mistake.
jen_dev: confirm by running: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id /hostedzone/hz-AAAA` and `aws route53 list-vpc-association-authorizations --hosted-zone-id /hostedzone/hz-BBBB` — also check the record-set for billing.api.* in each zone: `aws route53 list-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id /hostedzone/hz-AAAA --query "StartRecordName,ResourceRecordSets[?Name=='billing.api.private.example.com.']"`
sam_support: they pasted both record-sets. hz-AAAA has NO record for billing.api..., hz-BBBB has correct A -> 10.10.10.45. But when they query 10.0.1.2 (node-local cache) they get NXDOMAIN.
jen_dev: node-local DNS cache could be serving stale negative cache or forwarding to a resolver that lacks the right zone assoc. check `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=node-local-dns -o wide` and `kubectl logs <node-local-pod>` for cache hits. Also check CoreDNS `kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o yaml` for upstream forwarders.
mike_ops: also verify the VPC's resolver rules: `aws route53resolver list-resolver-rules --filters Name=VPCs,Values=vpc-22222` and that no outbound rule is hijacking example.com to an on-prem forwarder that doesn't know the private zone.
sam_support: customer ran `kubectl delete pod node-local-dns-abcde -n kube-system` and retested — still NXDOMAIN. They then queried the VPC resolver (`10.0.0.2`) directly and got the correct IP. So node-local is forwarding to the wrong resolver (10.0.1.2) which is returning NXDOMAIN because its resolver doesn't see the hosted-zone assoc.
alice_sre: sounds like their DHCP / VPC resolver setting points pods to node-local which forwards to the VPC's DHCP-provided resolver (should be .2), but they recently changed subnet route table to point to a shared forwarder (10.0.1.2) which lacks the association.
jen_dev: two-pronged remediation: 1) disassociate shared hosted zone from their prod VPC (if it was accidental) OR explicitly associate the correct prod hosted zone (hz-BBBB) with vpc-22222. 2) flip the node-local/CoreDNS forwarder back to the VPC resolver IPs or update forwarder to use the VPC resolver that knows the correct zone.
mike_ops: customer also saw TLS failures when curling the endpoint after they manually hardcoded the A record to the IP — `curl https://billing.api.private.example.com` -> `SSL: certificate subject name (shared-prod.example.com) does not match` — that's because the wrong hostname was served from the other backend. So even if they point to IP, SNI/cert mismatch will break.
sam_support: customer asked for a quick fix: we told them to disassociate hz-AAAA from vpc-22222 (they have permission to do so) and to flush node-local caches. They did `aws route53 disassociate-vpc-from-hosted-zone --hosted-zone-id /hostedzone/hz-AAAA --vpc VPCRegion=us-east-1,VPCId=vpc-22222` and then restarted node-local pods.
jen_dev: what's their post-change verification? show dig from pod and from node-local.
sam_support: after change: `dig @10.0.1.2 billing.api.private.example.com +short` -> 10.10.10.45; pod dig via node-local -> 10.10.10.45; curl succeeds and TLS validated. Customer confirmed incident resolved.
alice_sre: add checklist to runbook: - audit hosted zones across accounts when adding cross-account assoc - verify VPC association list before associating - ensure node-local/CoreDNS forwarder IPs point to resolvers that have the private zones - include cert/SNI check when switching DNS records.
dns_bot: Incident closed: tag #priv-dns #customer-acmecorp. :white_check_mark:
